problem:
$$
f(r,\theta )=⟨r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\text{_____}⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(r,\theta )$ parametrizes the surface defined in cylindrical polar coordinates as 
$4{r}^{2}-{z}^{2}=0$
for $z\ge 0.$ What is the third component of $f?$

feedback.problem:
$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,\text{_____}⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $r(u,v)$ parametrizes the surface defined in Cartesian coordinates as 
$\frac{x+y}{6}+\frac{z-1}{2}=\frac{1}{6}.$
 What is the third component of $r?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we write the equation of the surface in the form $z=f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x+y}{6}+\frac{z-1}{2} & =\frac{1}{6} \\ \frac{z-1}{2} & =\frac{1}{6}-\frac{x+y}{6} \\ \frac{z-1}{2} & =\frac{1-x-y}{6} \\ z & =\frac{4-x-y}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, a point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface has the corresponding position vector given by

$$
r=⟨x,\,y,\,z⟩=⟨x,\,y,\,\frac{4-x-y}{3}⟩.
$$

 

Finally, setting $x=u$ and $y=v,$ we obtain the vector function that parametrizes the surface:

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,\frac{4-u-v}{3}⟩
$$

Therefore, the third component of $r$ is $\frac{4-u-v}{3}.$
